element_tail.content: 1. Executive Overview
heading_path: 1. Executive Overview

element_tail.content:
The Kestrel-7 autonomous survey platform completed a twenty-six week deployment across three survey sites
during the 2031 operating season. Platform availability reached 94.6 percent of scheduled operating hours,
with a total of 412 completed survey runs and eighteen scheduled maintenance interventions.
heading_path: 1. Executive Overview

element_tail.content:
The platform demonstrated stable behaviour in all assigned operating conditions. The principal operational
findings are summarised below:
heading_path: 1. Executive Overview

element_tail.content: - Sensor drift remained within the calibrated budget for the full season.
heading_path: 1. Executive Overview

element_tail.content: - No unplanned power interruptions were recorded on the primary battery rail.
heading_path: 1. Executive Overview

element_tail.content: - All maintenance actions were completed within their scheduled windows.
heading_path: 1. Executive Overview

element_tail.content: - The mean time between maintenance interventions was 22.9 operating hours.
heading_path: 1. Executive Overview

element_tail.content:
The remainder of this report describes the calibration, power, deployment, maintenance, safety, and
performance characteristics that produced these results.
heading_path: 1. Executive Overview

element_tail.content: 2. Sensor Calibration
heading_path: 2. Sensor Calibration

element_tail.content:
Sensor calibration is performed before every deployment cycle. The Kestrel frame is calibrated against the
reference rig at the start of each cycle. The reference rig provides a known geometric baseline against which
frame alignment is verified.
heading_path: 2. Sensor Calibration

element_tail.content:
The inertial measurement unit (IMU) has a drift budget of 0.4 degrees per hour. Any drift measured above this
budget requires the gyro module to be replaced before the next deployment.
heading_path: 2. Sensor Calibration

element_tail.content:
The lidar array is aligned with the horizon prism using a two-point procedure. The two-point procedure is
repeated whenever the payload mast is removed or the horizon prism is replaced. Calibration is verified with
the reference rig at an ambient temperature within five degrees Celsius of the deployment temperature.
heading_path: 2. Sensor Calibration

2.question: How long does the survey team wait after landing before initiating the lidar sweep?

ranked_chunks.content:
4. Field Deployment

Field deployment follows a fixed sequence. After the platform is positioned at the survey origin, the survey
team waits four minutes after landing before initiating the lidar sweep. This settling period allows the inertial
measurement unit to reach thermal equilibrium.

5. Maintenance Schedule

Maintenance actions are scheduled from the platform's own operating-hour counter. The lidar array requires
recalibration every 250 operating hours. The inertial measurement unit and the horizon prism are serviced
every 500 operating hours. The primary battery rail and the communications module are inspected every 1000
operating hours.

1. Executive Overview

The Kestrel-7 autonomous survey platform completed a twenty-six week deployment across three survey sites
during the 2031 operating season. Platform availability reached 94.6 percent of scheduled operating hours,
with a total of 412 completed survey runs and eighteen scheduled maintenance interventions.

context.text:
6. Safety Procedures

The maximum permissible wind speed for deployment is 12 metres per second. Deployment is suspended
immediately when the measured wind speed exceeds this limit. A two-person rule applies to all deployments: a
single operator may not launch, recover, or service the platform.

4. Field Deployment

Deployment is suspended when the wind speed exceeds the limit stated in the safety procedures. The survey
team records the deployment start and end time for every survey run.
